parsedVerdict.reasoning:
The file is a domain file (it matches **/*.entity.ts), but it holds no domain rules. Its only content is database mapping:
- CustomBaseEntity extends TypeORM's BaseEntity. That base class is an active-record class: every subclass inherits save, remove and find methods. So all the entities that extend it (User, Role, Permission, EmailTemplate) carry persistence behaviour inside the domain layer.
- The id, createdAt and updatedAt fields use @PrimaryGeneratedColumn, @CreateDateColumn and @UpdateDateColumn. These set the column type ('timestamp'), the SQL default (() => 'CURRENT_TIMESTAMP') and the SQL onUpdate trigger ('CURRENT_TIMESTAMP').

Choosing column types, SQL defaults and how primary keys are generated is database-schema and persistence work, which belongs to the infrastructure layer. The rubric names persistence logic in a domain file as a failure. Whether the file may import TypeORM at all is out of scope. The failure here is about what the file does, not what it imports.

Confidence is moderate because annotated ORM entities are the usual NestJS pattern, even though they mix layers.
